prerequisites: Knowledge of statics and fundamentals of mechanics – forces, reactions, constraints, Newton’s laws. Familiarity with the following concepts is required: moment of a force at a point, balance/reduction of an arbitrary spatial force system, definitions of internal forces in a member, vector algebra and mass geometry.

Ability to calculate the following quantities: internal force in a member, moment of static and moment of inertia of composite figures and simple solids, the parallel and rotary transformation of the coordinate system.

learning_outcomes.text: Student knows: foundations of tensor analysis and its applications in the solid mechanics.
Student knows: limitations of solutions of geometrically linear structures, when to superimpose displacements, what is the stability of the compressed member and what load leads to its loss.
Student knows: the most useful failure criteria hypotheses and their applications.
Student has practical skills in: performing the parallel and rotational transformation as well as calculating the eigenvalues of the stress, strain or moment of inertia tensors.

Student has practical skills in: calculating of the stress and displacement in a member with a compact or a thin-walled cross-section loaded with tension–compression, torsion, shear or bending force as well as stress in welded, riveted, bolted joints.
Student has practical skills in: designing a member resistant to buckling in the elastic and elastic-plastic regions.
Social competencies: independent research and critical evaluation of the found sources.
Social competencies: objective evaluation of arguments, rational explanation and justification of the student’s viewpoint using knowledge of the strength of materials.
Social competencies: conforming to the academic principles.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Basic notions. Experimental foundations of the discipline. Strength design of straight members in tension and compression.
Stress theory.
Theory of strain. Engineering measurements of strain.
Physical relationships between stress and strain.
Torsion of circular shafts.
Torsion of members of arbitrary cross-section. Thin-walled members.
Shearing of joints.
Symmetric bending of straight members. Internal forces and stresses.
General case of bending. Unsymmetrical bending. Shearing centre.
Displacements in beams. Deflection line of a beam.
Buckling of members.
Strain energy, spherical and deviatoric parts of tensor, shear energy.
Failure criteria and combined modes of loading.
Energy methods for determining displacements in statically determinate and indeterminate member systems.
Stress concentration. Permissible stress. Factor of safety.
Strength design of straight members in tension and compression. Effect of temperature.
Statically indeterminate cases in stretching/compressing.
Plane stress. Mohr’s circle.
Engineering strain measurement.
Shafts in torsion – strength and stiffness.
Thin-walled members in torsion – strength and stiffness.
Written test.
Bending. Stress field.
General case of bending.
Displacements in beams. Deflection line of a beam.
Unsymmetrical bending. Shearing centre.
Buckling of compressed members.
Applications of failure criteria hypotheses.
Castigliano and Menabre-Castigliano theorem.
Written test.
teaching_methods: Lectures supported with audiovisual aids when necessary.
Self study and preparation for the exam.
assessment_rules: The lecture part is evaluated by a written and oral exam. The classes part is evaluated by an oral examination, written test 1, and written test 2.
degree: Mechanical Engineering and Machine Building (I level, full-time)
